newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba calls for strict Maastricht interpretation.
newsitem.headline: Buba calls for strict Maastricht interpretation.

text.p: The Bundesbank, calling for strict adherence to Maastricht Treaty criteria, warned against confusing politically-driven convergence of European bond yields with convergence of economic fundamentals.

In its monthly report for November, the Bundesbank sounded again familiar warnings about entering into European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) if the economic health of its participants was not sound.
"In order to keep the initial political dangers of the integration process at a minimum, a strict adherence to the Maastricht Treaty is to be pressed for."

The report noted that bond yields in Europe have narrowed in part because of speculation that political forces will lead EMU to start on schedule but said underlying economic factors will determine the success of EMU.
"It would be a heavy mortgage for the credibility of EMU monetary policy," the Bundesbank said of confusing politcal and economic reasons for yield convergence.
The bank also expressed disappointment that the difference between long- and short-term interest rates has remained large, saying the wide spread was in part due to EMU expecations.
According to monetary union time-tables, long-term German bonds would be repaid in euros, not the traditionally strong mark.

The Bundesbank said the steep yield curve reflected the view that "uncertainty or scepticism about interest and inflation rates is connected to European monetary union," adding their worries were most pronounced regarding fiscal convergence.
It said attempts at "creative accounting" of the fiscal criteria were increasingly being viewed critically.
